definition_zh: 装饰品；装饰物；装饰纹样；为场所增光的人或物；装饰音；仪式礼器；装饰、点缀（动词）
definition_en: a small object or added detail that decorates something; a person or thing that brings distinction; a musical flourish; a set of ceremonial vessels; also a verb meaning to adorn
core_image: 一只玻璃小球挂上圣诞树最低的枝条，整棵树因为这一点亮光就显出了节日的样子
scene: 圣诞树已经立好在客厅角落，彩球和细链正一层层挂上去，She lifts a glass ornament from the box and hooks it onto a low branch.
sceneCN: 这里 ornament 指「悬挂起来的小件装饰物」（第 1 个义项：单件装饰品）；句意为她从盒子里取出一只玻璃挂饰，挂到较低的枝条上。图中可辨识物件：立好的圣诞树、装挂饰的纸盒、玻璃球与细链。

pos.zh: 装饰品；装饰物；装饰音
装饰；点缀

derivatives.zh: 装饰；装饰品；整体装饰体系

senses.title: A small object kept for display
senses.titleCN: 为陈列而保留的小件装饰物
senses.definition: a small object, often hanging or standing, that is kept and shown because it makes a place look better
senses.definitionCN: 常为悬挂或摆放的小件物品，因能让场所更好看而被保留、陈列
senses.example: A single silver ornament hung at the centre of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 树的中央挂着一件银质小饰品。
senses.why: This is the concrete end of the word: Latin ornamentum named the fittings of a house or a person, and English narrowed that set down to one pretty object.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最具体的一端：拉丁 ornamentum 本指房屋或人的配备之物，英语把这一整组收窄成单独一件好看的物件。

senses.title: An added detail on a made object
senses.titleCN: 制成品表面上的附加纹样
senses.definition: a pattern, carving or inlay added to an object to make it more beautiful rather than more useful
senses.definitionCN: 为让物件更美而不是更有用而添加的图案、雕刻或镶嵌
senses.example: The brass clock is covered in engraved ornament.
senses.exampleCN: 这座黄铜钟上布满雕刻纹饰。
senses.why: Once the object itself is no longer the unit, the word can name any added surface detail, and the emphasis moves from the thing to the marking.
senses.whyCN: 当计量单位不再是物件本身，这个词就能指任何附加的表面细部，重心也从物件转到纹样。

senses.title: Decoration built into a building
senses.definition: a decorative feature of a building, such as a moulding, capital or carved panel, that is part of the structure
senses.definitionCN: 建筑上的装饰性构件，如线脚、柱头或雕刻板，本身属于结构的一部分
senses.example: The porch is enriched with stone ornament in a leaf pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 门廊以叶片纹样的石雕装饰增色。
senses.why: Architecture needed a word for decoration that is fixed in place, and ornament supplied it because the Latin noun already meant the fittings of a structure.
senses.whyCN: 建筑需要一个指固定不动的装饰的词，本词正好合用，因为拉丁名词本就是指建筑的配备件。

senses.title: A person who graces a group
senses.definition: a person whose presence or achievements bring credit to a place, profession or occasion
senses.definitionCN: 其在场或成就为某地、某行业或某场合带来荣誉的人
senses.example: The retired judge was an ornament to the small committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退休法官是那个小委员会的一大光彩。
senses.why: The figurative step treats social value as visible beauty: someone who makes a group look better is, in the old sense, a fitting.
senses.whyCN: 这一步比喻把社会价值当作可见的美：让群体显得更体面的人，按旧义就是一件合宜的配备之物。

senses.title: Adornment itself, not the thing
senses.definition: the quality or act of adorning, considered apart from any single object
senses.definitionCN: 脱离任何单件物品来看的装饰性质或装饰行为
senses.example: The carving was added for ornament, not for strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这道雕刻是为装饰而加，并非为了加固。
senses.why: English allows the noun to be a mass noun, so the word can name adornment in general and stand opposite to use or function.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个名词作不可数用法，于是它能泛指装饰，并与用途、功能相对。

senses.title: An added note that beautifies a line
senses.titleCN: 为旋律增色的附加音符
senses.definition: a grace note, trill or turn added to a melody to make it more elaborate
senses.definitionCN: 为使旋律更繁复而加入的倚音、颤音或回音
senses.example: The pianist added a small ornament at the end of each phrase.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家在每一乐句的结尾加了一个小装饰音。
senses.why: Music borrowed the idea directly: what is added for beauty rather than necessity is an ornament, and the term survived as a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 音乐直接借用了这一想法：为美而非为必需添加的东西就是装饰，这个说法作为术语沿用下来。

senses.title: Vessels and fittings of a ceremony
senses.titleCN: 仪式所用的器皿与陈设
senses.definition: the decorated vessels and furnishings used in a religious or state ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 宗教或国家仪式上使用的装饰性器皿与陈设
senses.example: The cathedral keeps its silver ornament locked in the treasury.
senses.exampleCN: 主教座堂把银质礼器锁在宝物室里。
senses.why: Here the older collective sense returns: ornament is not one pretty thing but the whole set of fittings proper to a solemn place.
senses.whyCN: 这里回归较古老的集合义：本词不是一件好看的东西，而是一个庄严场所应有的整套陈设。

senses.title: To decorate something (verb)
senses.definition: to decorate or embellish something, especially in a careful or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 装饰或点缀某物，尤指用心地、正式地加以修饰
senses.example: Fresh laurel ornamented the doorway for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 为这场典礼，新鲜的月桂装饰了门廊。
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin verb's active sense of fitting something out, and its stress falls on the last syllable, which sets it apart from the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁动词「为某物配齐装备」的主动义；重音落在末音节，与名词区分开来。

intro.en: Ornament comes from Latin ornamentum 'equipment, adornment', a noun built on the verb ornare 'to equip, fit out, adorn'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ornament 来自拉丁语 ornamentum「装备、装饰物」，由动词 ornare「装饰、配备」加名词后缀 -mentum 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ornare meant 'to equip, fit out, adorn'. It was used of preparing a person, a house or a ship for use, so adornment and equipment were the same act.
items.cn: ornare 意为「装备、配备、装饰」。它用于把人、房屋或船准备停当，所以装饰与配备在当时是同一个动作。

items.en: The suffix -mentum formed nouns of means or result, so ornamentum was the equipment or furnishing of something, and by extension its adornment.
items.cn: 后缀 -mentum 构成表示手段或结果的名词，因此 ornamentum 指某物的装备与陈设，进而指它的装饰。

items.en: Old French took the noun as ornement and kept both faces of it, the furnishing of a place and the beauty added to it.
items.cn: 古法语接受这个名词并把它变作自己的形式，两面都保留下来：场所的陈设，以及为之增添的美。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century; early uses covered church furnishing, military equipment and adornment generally.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪借入这个词；早期用法涵盖教堂陈设、军备以及一般意义上的装饰。

items.en: Later the noun narrowed to a single decorative object, and a verb ornament 'to adorn' grew beside it, with the stress moved to the final syllable.
items.cn: 后来名词收窄为单件装饰物，旁边又长出动词 ornament「装饰」，重音移到末音节。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin source of ornare is not established, so any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ornare 在拉丁语之前的来源并无定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式，而非实际书证。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to ornament, including one from another root; the second holds near synonyms that differ in whether they name an object, an act or a whole scheme.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近或音近的词，其中有一个来自别的词根；第二组是近义词，区别在于所指是一件物品、一个动作还是一整套方案。

entries.definition: Elaborately decorated; it goes back to the same Latin verb ornare, but it describes a style rather than an object.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰繁复的；同出拉丁动词 ornare，但描述的是风格而非物件。

entries.definition: Serving as decoration; formed from this noun with an adjective suffix, so it answers the question of what a thing is for.
entries.definitionCN: 作装饰用的；由本词加形容词后缀构成，回答的是「它作何用」。

entries.definition: Military supplies and guns; it comes from the same source as the word for a decree, not from ornare.
entries.definitionCN: 军械与火炮；与表示「法令」的词同源，与 ornare 无关。

entries.definition: The act or result of decorating, and a neutral cover term for anything added for beauty; it belongs to the decorare family, not the ornare family.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰的行为或结果，也是任何为美观而添加之物的中性统称；属 decorare 一族，与 ornare 一族不同源。

entries.definition: The act of adorning or the thing added; it comes from adorn, which is Latin adornare, ornare with the prefix ad-.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰的行为或添加之物；来自表示「装饰」的英语动词，其拉丁语形式由「装饰」词根加表示「向」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: A detail added to make something richer or more interesting, often in speech or writing as well as in design.
entries.definitionCN: 为使事物更丰富或更有趣而添加的细节，既用于设计与写作，也用于言谈。

entries.definition: A small ornament of little value; it names the object and implies cheapness, which this word does not.
entries.definitionCN: 价值不高的小饰物；指物件并含廉价之意，而本词不含此意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Ornare 'to equip' plus -mentum 'means or result' gives the fittings of a thing, and later its finery.
normal.cn: ornare「配备」加 -mentum「手段或结果」= 一件东西的配备，后来成了它的华饰。

normal.en: A ship's ornamenta were once its gear; the word still carries that old idea of fitting something out.
normal.cn: 船的 ornamenta 原本指它的索具装备；这个词至今仍带着「为某物配齐」的旧意。

normal.en: The noun puts the stress at the front and the verb puts it at the end; the shift marks the change of job.
normal.cn: 名词把重音放在前面，动词把重音放在末尾；重音的移动标记了词性的转换。

normal.en: Architects call a fixed decorative feature an ornament, never a decoration, because it is built into the fabric.
normal.cn: 建筑师把砌进本体的固定饰件称作装饰细部，而不说「装饰」，因为它属于结构本身。

normal.en: Christmas ornaments are small, many and hung, so the plural suits objects that arrive in sets.
normal.cn: 圣诞挂饰小而多、逐件悬挂，复数形式正适合成批出现的物件。

abstract.en: Picture one bright bead on a dark tree: the whole room changes because a small thing was added.
abstract.cn: 想象暗色圣诞树上的一颗亮珠：只因添了一件小东西，整个房间都变了。

abstract.en: Picture a plain doorway that becomes ceremonial the moment laurel is tied across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道普通的门，在系上一条月桂的那一刻变得庄重。

abstract.en: Picture a person who is of no use in the room but makes the room worth entering.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，在房间里并无用处，却让这房间值得走进去。

examples.en: She keeps a box of glass ornaments for the tree.
examples.cn: 她留着一盒玻璃挂饰，专供圣诞树用。

examples.en: The lintel carries a carved ornament of overlapping leaves.
examples.cn: 门楣上有一道叠叶纹样的雕刻装饰。

examples.en: Hosts ornament the table with branches and small candles.
examples.cn: 主人用枝条和小蜡烛装饰餐桌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，那门」——门口挂的那串小饰物，就是装饰品。拉丁 ornare 是「配备、装饰」，配上去的多余之物，正是装饰。名词重音在前，动词重音在后，读音也跟着换了身份。

root: 拉丁 ornare「装饰、配备」加名词后缀 -mentum「手段或结果」构成 ornamentum「装备、装饰物」，经古法语进入英语；名词指装饰物，动词指装饰。ornare 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，相关印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a single hanging object through surface detail, built ornament, a person who brings credit, adornment as such, a musical note and a set of ceremonial vessels, and end with the verb 'to adorn'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单件悬挂饰品出发，经过表面纹样、建筑饰件、为群体增光的人、装饰本身、音乐装饰音与仪式礼器，最后落在动词「装饰」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small bright thing added to a plain surface, so that the whole surface reads as cared for.
core.cn: 核心意象：在素净的表面上添一件小而亮的东西，整个表面因此显得被用心对待。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the concrete end of the word, a piece kept because it makes a place look better.
branches.cn: 物件：这个词最具体的一端，一件因能让场所更好看而被保留的东西。

branches.en: SURFACE AND STRUCTURE: the same idea moves from a marking on an object to a feature built into a building.
branches.cn: 表面与结构：同一想法从物件上的纹样移到砌进建筑的构件。

branches.en: PERSON AND QUALITY: adornment can be a human presence that brings credit, or the abstract act of adorning itself.
branches.cn: 人与性质：装饰可以是为群体增光的在场之人，也可以是抽象的装饰行为本身。

branches.en: SPECIALISED SETS: music keeps the added-for-beauty idea in a single note, while ceremony keeps the older collective sense of fittings.
branches.cn: 专门领域：音乐把「为美而添加」收在一个音符上，仪式则保留较早的「整套陈设」集合义。

branches.en: THE VERB: the act of fitting something out with beauty, with the stress moved to the last syllable.
branches.cn: 动词：为某物配齐美观之物的动作，重音移到末音节。

intro.en: Ornament is built from one Latin verb, one Latin noun suffix and a small English family, so it can be read piece by piece.
intro.cn: ornament 由一个拉丁动词、一个拉丁名词后缀和一小族英语派生词构成，可以逐块读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin ornare 'to equip, adorn' gives ornamentum and the English family; the suffix -mentum marks means or result, and English later added -al and -ation for quality and process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ornare「配备、装饰」衍生出 ornamentum 与英语这一族词；拉丁后缀 -mentum 表示手段或结果，英语后来又加表示性质与过程的后缀。

items.example: The verb describes the act of fitting something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述为某物配齐装备的动作。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the act of fitting out into the fittings themselves.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「配齐」的动作变成所配之物。

items.example: Latin used the noun for the fittings of a house, a ship or a person.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指房屋、船只或人的配备之物。

items.example: English kept both the noun and the later verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留了名词和后来出现的动词。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective of function.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示用途的形容词。

items.example: An ornamental feature is there to be looked at.
items.exampleCN: 装饰性构件之所以存在，是为了被人观看。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb or noun into a name for a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词或名词变成表示过程的名词。

items.meaning: the act or result of decorating, or the decoration as a whole
items.meaningCN: 装饰行为或结果；整体装饰
items.example: The word treats many ornaments as one system.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把许多装饰件当作一个体系来看。

derivatives.structure: ornament + -al (adjective suffix, from Latin -alis): the noun of a decorative thing shifts to an adjective of function
derivatives.meaning: serving as decoration rather than as structure
derivatives.meaningCN: 作装饰之用而非结构之用的

derivatives.structure: ornament + -ation (noun suffix, from Latin -atio): the single object shifts to the process and the collected result
derivatives.meaning: the act or system of decorating
derivatives.meaningCN: 装饰的行为或整体装饰体系

definition_zh: 鸟类学家；野外鸟类观察者；鸟类鉴定者；鸟类学著作的作者；鸟类标本与数据的整理者
definition_en: a person who studies birds in a scientific or systematic way, or who works professionally at identifying, recording, curating or protecting them
core_image: 天没亮，一个人蹲在雾里的芦苇边，笔记本上写满鸟名、时间与方位
scene: 天还没亮，志愿者在塘边支起细网，把每只刚取下来的小鸟交给桌后的人。 The ornithologist fitted a numbered band to each captured bird before releasing it.
sceneCN: 这里 ornithologist 是「环志工作者」（第 6 个义项：给鸟套上编号环并记录回收数据的鸟类学工作者）；句意为这位鸟类学工作者给每只捕获的鸟套上编号环，然后把它放走。

pos.zh: 鸟类学家；鸟类研究工作者；可数

senses.title: A Scientist Who Studies Birds
senses.titleCN: 鸟类学家（以研究鸟为业的人）
senses.definition: a researcher whose professional work is the scientific study of birds
senses.definitionCN: 以科学地研究鸟类为职业的研究者
senses.example: The ornithologist spent four years revising the classification of the genus.
senses.exampleCN: 这位鸟类学家花了四年修订该属的分类。
senses.why: -ist marks the person who practices a -logy, so the word's first sense is simply 'one who does ornithology'.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记从事某门 -logy 的人，因此这个词的第一义就是「做鸟类学的人」。

senses.title: A Field Observer and Recorder
senses.definition: a person whose work consists of walking set routes and writing down every bird seen or heard
senses.definitionCN: 以沿固定路线行走、记录所见所闻的每一只鸟为工作的人
senses.example: An ornithologist walked the same transect twice a week and logged every contact.
senses.exampleCN: 一位鸟类学工作者每周沿同一条样线走两次，记录下每一次接触。
senses.why: most bird evidence is gathered on foot at fixed hours, so the person's title attaches to the routine rather than to a laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 多数鸟类证据是在固定时段徒步采集的，因此这个称谓附着于日常路线，而非实验室。

senses.title: A Skilled Amateur Identifier
senses.titleCN: 业余但资深的鸟类鉴定者
senses.definition: a person with expert identification skill who is not employed as a researcher
senses.definitionCN: 具备专家级鉴定能力、但并非受雇研究者的人
senses.example: Though unpaid, she was the ornithologist everyone consulted about gulls.
senses.exampleCN: 虽然没有报酬，她却是大家遇到鸥类问题都要请教的鸟类学家。
senses.why: the title follows demonstrated skill rather than a salary, so a dedicated volunteer can wear it without a degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓跟的是已被证明的本领而非薪水，因此专注的志愿者没有学位也能担当。

senses.title: The Author of a Bird Study
senses.definition: the person who writes a regional or systematic account of birds
senses.definitionCN: 撰写某一地区或某一类群鸟类系统论述的人
senses.example: The ornithologist who wrote the 1922 volume never visited the island.
senses.exampleCN: 写出 1922 年那卷书的鸟类学家从未到过这座岛。
senses.why: before the word named a profession it named the author of an ornithology, and that sense survives in bibliographic writing.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词成为职业名之前，它先指一部鸟类学著作的作者，这一义项在书目写作中留存。

senses.title: A Curator of Study Skins
senses.definition: a person responsible for the care, labelling and loan of preserved bird specimens
senses.definitionCN: 负责保存鸟皮标本的养护、标注与外借的人
senses.example: The museum's ornithologist rehoused ten thousand study skins in new cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的鸟类学家把一万件鸟皮标本移入新标本柜。
senses.why: a collection is only usable if someone keeps its labels honest, so the title also belongs to the keeper of the cabinet.
senses.whyCN: 藏品只有靠人保证标签可靠才可用，因此这个称谓也属于看管标本柜的人。

senses.title: A Banding Worker
senses.definition: a person who catches birds, fits numbered rings or bands and files the recovery records
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉鸟类、套上编号环或腿环并归档回收记录的人
senses.example: The ornithologist opened the mist net well before first light.
senses.exampleCN: 这位鸟类学工作者在天亮前很久就张开了雾网。
senses.why: banding is the discipline's main way of following individual birds, and the person doing it is named by the field rather than by a degree.
senses.whyCN: 环志是该学科追踪个体鸟的主要手段，做这件事的人是按工作领域而非学位来称呼的。

senses.title: A Conservation Scientist for Birds
senses.definition: a researcher who turns bird survey data into advice on land use, turbines, or protected areas
senses.definitionCN: 把鸟类调查数据转化为土地使用、风机选址或保护区建议的研究者
senses.example: The ornithologist advised the agency on where to reroute the pipeline.
senses.exampleCN: 这位鸟类学家就管道改线位置向主管机构提供建议。
senses.why: when population counts are used to decide where things may be built, the researcher's title moves into applied work.
senses.whyCN: 当种群计数被用来决定何处可以施工，研究者的称谓便进入了应用工作。

senses.title: An Expert on Bird Song
senses.titleCN: 凭鸣声辨识鸟类的专家
senses.definition: a person able to identify species by call alone, without seeing the bird
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭鸣叫就能识别物种、不必看到鸟的人
senses.example: A patient ornithologist can name a warbler from four notes.
senses.exampleCN: 有耐心的鸟类学家凭四个音就能叫出一只柳莺的名字。
senses.why: in dense cover the ear replaces the eye, so a specialised skill becomes a recognised identity within the field.
senses.whyCN: 在茂密灌丛里耳朵取代了眼睛，于是某种专门技能在业内成为一种被认可的身份。

intro.en: Ornithologist is ornithology plus -ist, the agent suffix that names a person who practices something; ornithology itself is Greek ornis 'bird' (genitive ornithos) plus -logia. The Greek agent suffix was -istēs, which reached English through Latin -ista and French -iste.
intro.cn: ornithologist 是 ornithology 加 -ist，这个施事后缀用来称呼从事某事的人；ornithology 本身是希腊 ornis「鸟」（属格 ornithos）加 -logia。希腊语中的施事后缀为 -istēs，经拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 进入英语。

items.en: Ornis, genitive ornithos, is the Greek noun for 'bird'; it supplies the first element of both ornithology and ornithologist.
items.cn: ornis 的属格为 ornithos，是希腊语中表「鸟」的名词；它同时提供 ornithology 与 ornithologist 的第一成分。

items.en: Logos 'word, account, reason' produced -logia, the suffix for a reasoned study; the discipline's name therefore means 'account of birds'.
items.cn: logos「言说、叙述、道理」产生后缀 -logia，表示成体系的研究；学科名因此意为「关于鸟的论述」。

items.en: The Greek agent suffix -istēs named the person who does what the base word describes, and it passed into Latin as -ista and into English as -ist.
items.cn: 希腊施事后缀 -istēs 指从事词基所述之事的人，后经拉丁 -ista 进入英语作 -ist。

items.en: Ornithologia was coined in early modern scientific Latin from the Greek pieces; its usual attribution to Aldrovandi's Ornithologiae (1599) is a general view, not a documented certainty.
items.cn: ornithologia 由希腊成分在近代早期科学拉丁语中造出；通常归于阿尔德罗万迪 1599 年的《鸟类学》，这是一般看法，而非有文献确证的事实。

items.en: English ornithologist is recorded from the eighteenth century, shortly after ornithology itself entered the language; the earliest citation is not firmly fixed.
items.cn: 英语 ornithologist 自 18 世纪有记录，晚于 ornithology 进入英语不久；最早的书证尚未确定。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first date of ornithologist and the pre-Greek origin of ornis both remain open; only the Greek stem plus the agent suffix is securely established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ornithologist 的确切首见年代与 ornis 在希腊语之前的来源都仍无定论；可以确定的是希腊词干加施事后缀这一层。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes: two share the ornithology base, two merely carry a -ist ending. Group two sets the person beside the nearby roles, from hobbyist to general scientist.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词：两个共享 ornithology 词基，两个只是同样带 -ist 结尾。第二组把这个身份放在从爱好者到通才科学家的邻近角色之间。

entries.definition: The discipline itself, built on the same two Greek pieces; it names the study, while ornithologist names the person.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身，由同样的两个希腊成分构成；它指这门研究，而 ornithologist 指人。

entries.definition: The adjective of the field, describing journals and methods rather than a worker; the base is shared with ornithologist.
entries.definitionCN: 该领域的形容词，描述期刊与方法而非工作者；与 ornithologist 共享词基。

entries.definition: From Greek opsis 'sight' plus metron 'measure': a person who measures vision; the ending resembles -ologist but the root is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 opsis「视觉」加 metron「测量」：测量视力的人；结尾像 -ologist，但词根无关。

entries.definition: Geo- 'earth' plus -logist: a student of rocks; it shows that -ologist is a productive pattern, not evidence of a shared root.
entries.definitionCN: geo-「大地」加 -logist：研究岩石的人；这说明 -ologist 是能产模式，并不证明词根相同。

entries.definition: A person who watches birds for pleasure; an ornithologist may do the same, but is expected to produce records or research.
entries.definitionCN: 以观鸟为乐的人；ornithologist 也可能这样做，但被期待产出记录或研究成果。

entries.definition: An American word for an active birdwatcher who keeps lists; it marks a hobby identity rather than a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 美式说法，指积极观鸟并记录名录的人；标记的是爱好身份而非职业。

entries.definition: A person who studies living things in the field across groups; ornithologist narrows that role to one class.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外研究各类生物的人；ornithologist 把这个角色收窄到一个纲。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies relationships between organisms and their surroundings; some ecologists work on birds without being ornithologists.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境关系的科学家；有些生态学家研究鸟，但并非鸟类学家。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real agent suffix, the real Greek stem and the real institutional roles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的施事后缀、真实的希腊词干与真实的机构角色。

normal.en: ornith- 'bird' + -o- + -logy 'study' + -ist 'person': the whole word is a job description.
normal.cn: ornith-「鸟」+ -o- + -logy「学」+ -ist「人」：整个词就是一句职务说明。

normal.en: -ist marks the doer, exactly as in biologist and geologist, so the ending is a pattern rather than a root.
normal.cn: -ist 标记执行者，正如 biologist 与 geologist，因此这个结尾是模式而非词根。

normal.en: Real roles fix the senses: field, museum and conservation ornithologist.
normal.cn: 真实角色固定了各义项：野外、博物馆与保护鸟类学家。

normal.en: The base word is ornithology, so anyone called an ornithologist is assumed to know the discipline's literature.
normal.cn: 词基是 ornithology，因此被称为 ornithologist 的人被假定熟悉该学科的文献。

normal.en: Family: ornithology, ornithological, ornithologically, palaeornithologist.
normal.cn: 同族词：ornithology、ornithological、ornithologically、palaeornithologist。

abstract.en: Picture a knee-high notebook open in the dark, a headlamp angled down at the page.
abstract.cn: 想象天还黑着，一本齐膝高的笔记本摊开，头灯的光斜照在纸页上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer of skins whose labels only one person can vouch for.
abstract.cn: 想象一柜鸟皮标本，只有一个人能为其标签作保。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a bird, a ring on the tarsus, a stopwatch running.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手托着鸟，跗跖上套着环，秒表在走。

examples.en: Two ornithologists independently described the same subspecies.
examples.cn: 两位鸟类学家各自独立地描述了同一个亚种。

examples.en: The park hired an ornithologist to run its breeding survey.
examples.cn: 公园聘请了一位鸟类学家主持繁殖调查。

examples.en: As an ornithologist, he was more at home in a marsh than in a lecture hall.
examples.cn: 作为鸟类学家，他在沼泽里比在讲堂里更自在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「奥尼索罗吉斯特」——「奥尼」是鸟，「罗吉」是学，「斯特」是人 → 研究鸟的人

root: ornithology + -ist（希腊施事后缀 -istēs，经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste 进入英语）。ornithology 为希腊 ornis「鸟」（属格 ornithos）+ -logia「对……的论述、研究」。英语 ornithologist 自 18 世纪有记录，确切首见年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses answer one question: who is doing the bird work? The answer may be a salaried researcher, a route walker, a gifted amateur, an author, a curator, a bander, an adviser or an ear-trained identifier.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：是谁在做与鸟有关的工作？答案可以是受薪研究者、走样线的人、有天赋的业余者、作者、标本管理者、环志者、顾问，或靠耳朵辨鸟的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person crouching at dawn with a notebook open on one knee.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时分，一个人蹲着，笔记本摊在膝上。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND ITS AUTHOR: the researcher, and the writer who sets the knowledge down.
branches.cn: 知识及其作者：研究者，以及把知识写定的人。

branches.en: SKILL WITHOUT A PAYSLIP: the route walker and the unpaid expert the others consult.
branches.cn: 没有薪水的本领：走样线的人，以及众人请教的业余专家。

branches.en: THE CABINET KEEPER: someone must vouch for every label in the drawer.
branches.cn: 标本柜看守：抽屉里每张标签都必须有人作保。

branches.en: FOLLOWING AND PROTECTING: a ring on the leg, then advice on where to build.
branches.cn: 追踪与保护：腿上的环，随后是关于施工地点的建议。

branches.en: THE EAR AS INSTRUMENT: in cover, hearing replaces sight.
branches.cn: 耳朵作仪器：在灌丛里，听觉取代视觉。

intro.en: Ornithologist adds one more piece to the discipline's name: the agent suffix that says 'the person who'. Everything else is shared with ornithology.
intro.cn: ornithologist 在学科名之后再接一段：表示「做这件事的人」的施事后缀。其余部分与 ornithology 共用。

latinIntro.en: Greek ornis (genitive ornithos) and logos supply the stem and the suffix -logia; the agent suffix -istēs came through Latin -ista and French -iste.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 ornis（属格 ornithos）与 logos 提供词干与后缀 -logia；施事后缀 -istēs 经拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 传来。

items.structure: ornis (Greek noun, third declension, genitive ornithos)
items.example: The stem ornith- carries 'bird' through the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 ornith- 在整个词族中承载「鸟」义。

items.example: The -o- joins ornith- to the suffix that follows.
items.exampleCN: 这个 -o- 把 ornith- 与后面的后缀连接起来。

items.meaning: the study or reasoned account of
items.meaningCN: 对……的研究或成体系论述
items.example: Ornithology is the study of birds.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类学就是对鸟的研究。

items.structure: -istēs (Greek agent suffix, via Latin -ista and French -iste)
items.meaning: a person who practices or studies something
items.example: The suffix turns the field into the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学科变成从事该学科的人。

items.example: She trained in ornithology before moving into conservation.
items.exampleCN: 她在转入保护工作之前受过鸟类学训练。

items.example: The ornithologist checked the ageing of the specimen.
items.exampleCN: 这位鸟类学家核对了标本的年龄鉴定。

items.meaning: relating to the study of birds
items.example: The ornithological record goes back to 1870.
items.exampleCN: 这份鸟类学记录可追溯至 1870 年。

items.example: The palaeornithologist measured the fossil humerus.
items.exampleCN: 古鸟类学家测量了这块化石肱骨。

definition_zh: 正统的；正宗的；传统的
definition_en: following the accepted or officially correct set of beliefs and methods
core_image: 一条被无数脚踩得发亮的旧路，所有脚印都朝着同一个方向
scene: 学校里只教这一种写法，别的写法一律算错。The school teaches only one way to write it, and every other way is marked wrong, so the method has become orthodox.
sceneCN: 这里 orthodox 指公认的正统做法（第 3 个义项：公认方法）；句意为学校只教这一种写法，别的都算错，这套方法已成正统。

pos.zh: 正统的；正宗的；传统的

senses.title: Correct in doctrine
senses.definition: holding the beliefs that a church has declared correct
senses.definitionCN: 持守教会宣告为正确的信仰
senses.example: The council ruled that his teaching was not orthodox.
senses.exampleCN: 会议裁定他的教导不合正统。
senses.why: The word was born in religious argument, where correct opinion had a single judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词生于宗教争论，那里的「正确意见」只有一个裁判。

senses.title: Conventional in belief
senses.definition: believing what most people in one's circle believe
senses.definitionCN: 相信自己所处圈子里多数人所信的
senses.example: It was orthodox in that town to distrust the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个镇上，不信任铁路是正统观念。
senses.why: Here the judge is no longer a church but a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这里的裁判不再是教会，而是人群。

senses.title: The accepted method
senses.definition: the way of doing something that a profession treats as standard
senses.definitionCN: 某个行业视为标准的做法
senses.example: Surgery by keyhole is now orthodox for this operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这种手术如今以微创为正统做法。
senses.why: Practice, not doctrine, decides what is orthodox here.
senses.whyCN: 这里决定正统的是实践，而不是教义。

senses.title: Mainstream medicine
senses.definition: the medicine taught in universities and tested in trials, as against alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 大学所教、经试验检验的医学，与替代疗法相对
senses.example: She tried orthodox treatment before the herbal one.
senses.exampleCN: 她先试正统治疗，再试草药。
senses.why: The word draws a line, and the line is drawn by institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词画一条线，而线由机构来画。

senses.title: Traditional in art
senses.definition: following the established forms of a tradition rather than breaking them
senses.definitionCN: 沿袭传统的既定形式而不去打破
senses.example: His early work was orthodox, and only later did he loosen the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期作品很传统，后来才放松线条。
senses.why: In art the word can be faint praise: correct, and a little late.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术里，这个词可能是淡淡的贬意：正确，却晚了一步。

senses.title: Mainstream in policy
senses.definition: the economic or political thinking that the powerful currently accept
senses.definitionCN: 当权者目前接受的经济或政治思路
senses.example: Orthodox economics predicted a quick recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 主流经济学预测会迅速复苏。
senses.why: What is orthodox in one decade is often heterodox in the next.
senses.whyCN: 一个十年的正统，常常是下一个十年的异端。

senses.title: Conforming in behaviour
senses.definition: behaving in the way that is expected, without surprise
senses.definitionCN: 以别人期待的方式行事，不出意外
senses.example: He led an orthodox life and was never mentioned in the papers.
senses.exampleCN: 他过着循规蹈矩的生活，从未上过报纸。
senses.why: The word moves from ideas to habits, and loses most of its edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从观念移到习惯，也失去了大部分锋芒。

senses.title: Strictly by the book
senses.definition: keeping every detail of an established rule, even where it costs
senses.definitionCN: 连细节都守住既定规则，即使要付代价
senses.example: The monastery remained orthodox even about the hour of prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 那座修道院连祈祷的时辰都严守正统。
senses.why: Here correctness is exact and expensive, which is why the word can sound severe.
senses.whyCN: 这里的正确精确而昂贵，所以这个词听起来可以很严厉。

intro.en: Orthodox joins a Greek word for straight to a Greek word for opinion: right belief, judged by whoever holds the straight line.
intro.cn: orthodox 把一个意为「直」的希腊词与一个意为「意见」的希腊词接起来：正确信念，由握着那条直线的人来判定。

items.en: Orthos meant 'straight, upright, correct', the same idea that gives English orthodontics.
items.cn: orthos 意为「直的、正的、正确的」，与英语 orthodontics 里的概念相同。

items.en: Doxa meant 'opinion, what seems true', a weaker word than knowledge.
items.cn: doxa 意为「意见、看来如此」，比「知识」弱。

items.en: Orthodoxos meant 'of right opinion', first used of Christian teachers who held the accepted faith.
items.cn: orthodoxos 意为「意见正确的」，最初用于持守公认信仰的基督教教师。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, during arguments about the Reformation.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪宗教改革争论中借入此词。

items.en: Modern English applies it to medicine, economics and art, wherever a profession has a standard.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于医学、经济学与艺术，凡是行业有标准的地方。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ortho- prefix; the near-meaning group separates belief, custom, mainstream and doctrine.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ortho- 前缀；近义组把「信念」「习俗」「主流」与「教义」分开。

entries.definition: the accepted belief or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 被接受的信念或标准。

entries.definition: in an accepted way.
entries.definitionCN: 以正统的方式。

entries.definition: not following the accepted way.
entries.definitionCN: 不循正统的。

entries.definition: the straightening of teeth.
entries.definitionCN: 牙齿矫正术。

entries.definition: following what is usual.
entries.definitionCN: 依循常规的。

entries.definition: accepted by the majority.
entries.definitionCN: 被多数接受的。

entries.definition: handed down and kept.
entries.definitionCN: 沿袭下来的。

entries.definition: relating to official teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 与官方教义有关的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a worn path whose ruts all run one way.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一条磨亮的旧路，车辙都朝同一方向」的画面。

normal.en: Ortho- means straight: orthodox is a straight opinion, the one that does not lean off the line.
normal.cn: ortho- 意为「直」：orthodox 是「直的意见」，不偏线的那一种。

normal.en: Think of a path worn bright by everyone walking the same way.
normal.cn: 想象一条被众人同向踩亮的路径。

normal.en: Ortho-dox: straight plus opinion, the two Greek pieces are both visible in the spelling.
normal.cn: ortho-dox：直加意见，两个希腊部件在拼写里都看得见。

normal.en: Say AW-thuh-doks; the first syllable carries the straight line.
normal.cn: 读成 AW-thuh-doks，第一个音节带着那条直线。

normal.en: Pair it with unorthodox: the prefix simply steps off the path.
normal.cn: 把它和 unorthodox 配对：前缀只是从路上迈开一步。

abstract.en: Orthodoxy is a choice that has forgotten it was a choice.
abstract.cn: 正统是一个忘了自己曾是选择的决定。

abstract.en: Every profession draws its own straight line, and calls the line correct.
abstract.cn: 每个行业都画出自己的直线，并把那条线叫作正确。

abstract.en: To be orthodox is safe and slightly late; to be unorthodox is to pay for the earlier step.
abstract.cn: 正统是安全而略晚；非正统是为早迈的那一步付账。

examples.en: The school teaches one way to write it, and the method has become orthodox.
examples.cn: 学校只教一种写法，这套方法已成正统。

examples.en: Surgery by keyhole is now orthodox for this operation.
examples.cn: 这种手术如今以微创为正统做法。

examples.en: Orthodox economics predicted a quick recovery.
examples.cn: 主流经济学预测会迅速复苏。

dict_mnemonic.text: ortho（正）+ dox（意见）：持有正确意见的，就是「正统的」。

root: 希腊语 orthodoxos（意见正确的），由 orthos（正）与 doxa（意见）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all place a straight line somewhere: in a creed, a town, a trade, a clinic, a studio, a ministry, a habit and a monastery.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在某处画一条直线：信条里、小镇里、行业里、诊所里、画室里、部里、习惯里与修道院里。

core.en: THE WORN PATH EVERYONE FOLLOWS
core.cn: 所有人都在走的那条磨亮的旧路

chain: THE RULE FORGETS IT WAS A CHOICE

branches.en: A creed held exactly and a rule kept to the letter.
branches.cn: 严格持守的信条与守到字句的规则。

branches.en: A town's common belief and a life lived without surprise.
branches.cn: 小镇的共同信念与不出意外的人生。

branches.en: A trade's standard method and a clinic's approved cure.
branches.cn: 行业的标准做法与诊所认可的治疗。

branches.en: Tradition followed in art until it becomes faint praise.
branches.cn: 艺术中沿袭传统，直到它变成淡淡的褒贬。

branches.en: The thinking the powerful currently accept.
branches.cn: 当权者目前接受的思路。

intro.en: The ortho- family means straight: orthodox is a straight opinion, orthodontics straight teeth, orthography straight writing.
intro.cn: ortho- 词族意为「直」：orthodox 是直的意见，orthodontics 是直牙，orthography 是正写法。

latinIntro.en: Greek orthos supplies the line and doxa supplies the opinion; the opposite prefix hetero- supplies the other opinion.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 orthos 提供直线，doxa 提供意见；相反的前缀 hetero- 提供另一种意见。

definition_zh: 否则；不然；在其他方面；除此之外；以别的方式
definition_en: in a different way, in other respects, or as the other result that follows if something does not happen
core_image: 一条路在岔口分成两支，一块木牌倒在左边，指向右边的那条路几乎没人走过
scene: 末班车的时间已经过了，站台上只剩一个人，他看了看表，又看了看暗下来的街口。You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
sceneCN: 这里的 otherwise 是「否则、不然」（第 1 个义项：如果不这样，就会有另一种结果）；句意为你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。图中可辨识物件：站台、手表、暗下的街口。

pos.zh: 否则；不然；在其他方面；以别的方式
否则；不然

derivatives.zh: otherwise 的前半部分，来自古英语形容词 other，义为「另一个；别的」
由 other 加 -ness 构成，义为「他者性；异质性」
由 other 与 world 复合，再加 -ly 构成，义为「超凡脱俗的」

senses.title: If not this, then something else will happen
senses.definition: used to say what will happen if the action just mentioned is not taken
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出若不做刚提到的那件事，就会出现另一种结果
senses.example: You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。
senses.why: The word began as an Old English phrase meaning in other ways, so the second clause describes the other way things can go.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一句古英语短语，意为「以别的方式」，所以后一个分句说的就是事情可能走的另一种方式。

senses.title: In other respects, apart from what was just said
senses.definition: used to add that something is true apart from the one point already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充说明，除了刚才提到的那一点之外，其他方面是成立的
senses.example: The room is small but otherwise comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间虽小，其他方面却舒适。
senses.why: If the phrase means in other ways, it can also mean with regard to other matters, and that is how it moves from a condition to an exception.
senses.whyCN: 既然这句话意为「以别的方式」，它也就能指「就其他事情而言」，于是从假设的条件转成了例外的补充。

senses.title: In a different way, not like that
senses.definition: in another manner, especially when the manner just thought of was not possible
senses.definitionCN: 以另一种方式，尤指刚想到的那种方式并不可行时
senses.example: There was no choice; he could not have acted otherwise.
senses.exampleCN: 当时别无选择，他不可能有别的做法。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives intact here: otherwise simply says by another way, without implying any condition or exception.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思在这里完好地保留下来：otherwise 只说明「用另一种方式」，既不表条件，也不表例外。

intro.en: Otherwise is a frozen Old English phrase, on other wise, meaning in other ways; the two words fused into one adverb, and English later also used it as a conjunction.
intro.cn: otherwise 是一句凝固下来的古英语短语，原文意为「以别的方式」；两个词合成一个副词，英语后来又把它用作连词。

items.en: Other came from Old English oþer, meaning the second of two or simply a different one.
items.cn: other 来自古英语 oþer，意为两者中的另一个，或只是「不同的那一个」。

items.en: Wise was an old noun for manner or way, unrelated to the adjective meaning clever, and it survives in words such as likewise.
items.cn: wise 是表示方式、样子的古老名词，与表示「聪明」的形容词无关，它还活在 likewise 这类词里。

items.en: The phrase on oþre wisan meant in other ways, and it was used to describe an alternative course of action.
items.cn: 短语 on oþre wisan 意为「以别的方式」，用来描述另一种做法。

items.en: Middle English wrote the phrase as a single word, otherwise, and widened it to mean in other respects as well.
items.cn: 中古英语把这句短语写成一个词 otherwise，并把意思扩展到「在其他方面」。

items.en: Modern English uses otherwise as an adverb and a conjunction, with fixed phrases such as or otherwise and otherwise known as.
items.cn: 现代英语让 otherwise 兼作副词与连词，并有 or otherwise、otherwise known as 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on other and its family; the near-meaning group collects ways of naming an alternative.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 other 及其词族的词；近义组收表示「另一种选择」的说法。

entries.definition: A different person or thing, or the second of two.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的人或物，或两者中的另一个。

entries.definition: One more, or a different one.
entries.definitionCN: 再一个，或另一个不同的。

entries.definition: The state of being different from what is familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 与熟悉之物不同的状态。

entries.definition: More concerned with a spiritual world than with daily life.
entries.definitionCN: 更关注精神世界而非日常生活的。

entries.definition: Other than what has been mentioned, or in addition.
entries.definitionCN: 除已提到的之外，或另外。

entries.definition: As another possible choice or option.
entries.definitionCN: 作为另一种可能的选择。

entries.definition: A phrase warning of a bad result if something is not done.
entries.definitionCN: 警告若不照做就会有坏结果的短语。

normalIntro.en: Otherwise is a whole Old English phrase squeezed into one word, so its hooks keep the picture of a second way of doing something.
normalIntro.cn: otherwise 是一整句古英语短语被压成一个词，所以记忆钩子保留「做同一件事的第二种方式」的画面。

normal.en: The word is on other wise in Old English, literally in other ways, and the modern spelling simply fuses the pieces.
normal.cn: 这个词在古英语里写作 on other wise，字面就是「以别的方式」，现代拼写只是把几块合在了一起。

normal.en: Wise here is an old noun for manner, not the adjective for clever, which is why otherwise has nothing to do with being smart.
normal.cn: 这里的 wise 是表示方式的古老名词，而不是表示「聪明」的形容词，所以 otherwise 与聪明无关。

normal.en: The same -wise family gives likewise and clockwise, both of which name a way of doing or going.
normal.cn: 同一个 -wise 词族还给出 likewise 与 clockwise，两者都指做事或行进的方式。

normal.en: Otherwise known as is the fixed phrase for a second name, and or otherwise pairs with or to cover remaining cases.
normal.cn: otherwise known as 是表示「另一个名字」的固定说法，而 or otherwise 与 or 连用，覆盖剩下的情况。

normal.en: As a conjunction it joins two clauses: do this, otherwise that will happen, which is why it often sits mid-sentence.
normal.cn: 作连词时它连接两个分句：做这个，否则就会那样，所以它常出现在句子中间。

abstract.en: A word that means in other ways quietly admits that every choice closes off another path.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「以别的方式」的词，默默承认每个选择都关上了另一条路。

abstract.en: The second name of a place or person is often hidden behind otherwise known as, a phrase doing the work of a footnote.
abstract.cn: 一个地方或一个人的第二个名字，常常藏在 otherwise known as 后面，这个短语干着脚注的活。

abstract.en: To say a thing is fine otherwise is to hold the good and the bad in one short sentence.
abstract.cn: 说一件东西除此之外都不错，就是用一句很短的话同时握住好与坏。

examples.en: You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
examples.cn: 你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。

examples.en: The room is small but otherwise comfortable.
examples.cn: 这个房间虽小，其他方面却舒适。

examples.en: There was no choice; he could not have acted otherwise.
examples.cn: 当时别无选择，他不可能有别的做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外兹」——阿德偏向外面走，另选了一条路；记住 otherwise 是否则、以别的方式。

root: 由古英语短语 on oþre wisan（以别的方式）凝固成一个词，其中 oþer 意为「另一个」，wīse 意为「方式」；这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

sensesIntro.en: The core is another way; the senses divide by a condition, by other respects, and by the plain sense of doing something differently.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「另一种方式」；义项按假设的条件、其他方面，以及「以不同方式做事」的本义分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road forking at a signpost, one board fallen flat while the other path stands almost unused.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在岔口分成两支，一块木牌倒在左边，指向右边的那条路几乎没人走过。

branches.en: a platform after the last train has gone
branches.cn: 末班车开走后的站台

branches.en: a small room that is pleasant in every other way
branches.cn: 除面积之外都让人满意的一间小屋

branches.en: a path that could have been taken instead
branches.cn: 本可以改走的那一条路

branches.en: the same word for a condition and an alternative
branches.cn: 同一个词，既表示条件，也表示另一种选择

branches.en: other respects and other ways belong to one phrase
branches.cn: 「其他方面」与「别的方式」出自同一个短语

intro.en: The word is a frozen Old English phrase made of the adjective for other and the noun for manner, now written together as one adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是一句凝固的古英语短语，由表示「别的」的形容词与表示「方式」的名词组成，如今合写成一个副词。

latinIntro.en: Otherwise is built entirely from Old English words, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound.
latinIntro.cn: otherwise 完全由古英语词构成，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: in the direction of a clock

definition_zh: 盎司；少量；一点点；一丝
definition_en: a unit of weight of about twenty-eight grams, with a heavier troy form used for precious metals; also a very small amount or the slightest trace of a quality
core_image: 旧药铺柜台上的一台小铜天平，一端放着待称的小块黄油，另一端是小小的砝码
scene: 旧药铺的柜台上摆着一台小铜天平，药剂师把一小块黄油放上砝码盘，铜指针慢慢停住。The old recipe asks for one ounce of butter and a pinch of salt.
sceneCN: 这里 ounce 是「盎司」（第 1 个义项：常衡重量单位）；句意为老配方要一盎司黄油加一撮盐，画面是药铺柜台上那台停住的小铜天平。

pos.zh: 盎司；少量；一丝

derivatives.zh: 由 ounce 与 force 复合而成，义为「盎司力」，英制力的单位
由 inch 与 ounce 复合而成，义为「英寸盎司」，英制扭矩单位
由 fluid 与 ounce 复合而成，义为「液量盎司」，用于量液体容积

senses.title: A unit of weight equal to about twenty-eight grams
senses.definition: a unit of weight used in ordinary trade, equal to one sixteenth of a pound or about 28.35 grams
senses.definitionCN: 用于一般贸易的重量单位，等于十六分之一磅，约二十八点三五克
senses.example: Add four ounces of flour to the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 往碗里加四盎司面粉。
senses.why: Latin uncia named a twelfth part of a larger unit, so the word began as a fraction cut off from something bigger; trade later fixed that fraction into the everyday ounce of sixteen to the pound.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 uncia 本指某一较大单位的十二分之一，所以这个词一开始是「从大单位切下的一份」；后来贸易把这个分数固定成十六分之一磅的日常盎司，分数观念就变成了具体的称重单位。

senses.title: A troy unit used for precious metals
senses.definition: a unit of weight of about 31.1 grams, used for gold, silver and other precious metals
senses.definitionCN: 约三十一点一克的重量单位，用于黄金、白银等贵金属
senses.example: Gold is traded by the troy ounce on world markets.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金在国际市场上按金衡盎司交易。
senses.why: The older twelve-part division survived in the bullion trade after ordinary goods moved to a sixteen-part pound, so one name ended up covering two slightly different weights.
senses.whyCN: 日常货物改用十六分之一磅之后，旧式十二分之一的分法仍在金银交易里活着；同一个名字于是同时指两种略不相同的重量，贵金属这一支保留了更重的古制。

senses.title: A very small quantity
senses.definition: a very small amount of something, often used to stress how little is left or present
senses.definitionCN: 某物极少的一点，常用于强调所剩或所有之少
senses.example: There was not an ounce of sugar left in the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子里一点糖都不剩了。
senses.why: An ounce sits near the bottom of a kitchen scale, so the name of the smallest readable weight drifts easily into a word for a scrap of anything.
senses.whyCN: 盎司落在厨房秤刻度的最低处，于是这个「最小可读重量」的名称很容易滑成「随便一点什么」的说法；义项由称量的下限转向数量上的极小。

senses.title: The slightest trace of a quality
senses.definition: a small but real amount of a feeling or quality, as in an ounce of courage or not an ounce of sense
senses.definitionCN: 某种情感或品质虽少却真实的一点，如「一丝勇气」或「毫无理智」
senses.example: He did not show an ounce of regret for what he had done.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己做过的事没有表现出一丝悔意。
senses.why: The smallest weight is borrowed to weigh what cannot be put on a scale, so an ounce of a quality means just enough of it to count.
senses.whyCN: 最小的重量被借去称无法放上天平的东西，所以「一丝某种品质」就是刚好够算数的那一点；这次转移靠的是用称重词去量看不见的性情。

intro.en: Ounce descends from a Latin word for a twelfth part, and the same source also gave English inch, which is why a weight and a length share a name.
intro.cn: ounce 上溯自一个表示「十二分之一」的拉丁词，同一来源还给出了英语的 inch，所以一种重量与一种长度共用一段来历。

items.en: Uncia named a twelfth part of a pound or of any larger unit, and it is also the source of the English inch.
items.cn: uncia 指一磅或任何较大单位的十二分之一，也是英语 inch 的来源。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin word to unce, the form English borrowed for a small weight.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词缩为 unce，英语借入时用它指一种小重量。

items.en: Middle English kept the word for a small weight and for a twelfth part, and merchants used it alongside the pound.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指小重量，也指十二分之一，商人们把它与磅并用。

items.en: When the sixteen-ounce pound became standard for ordinary goods, the older twelve-part unit stayed in the bullion trade, so one name covered two weights.
items.cn: 当十六盎司为一磅的常衡制成为普通货物的标准，旧的十二进制单位仍留在金银交易中，同一个名字于是覆盖了两种重量。

items.en: Modern English uses ounce for the everyday measure, the troy measure for metals, and figuratively for a very small amount of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ounce 指日常重量、贵金属的金衡重量，也引申指任何东西的极小量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin twelfth-part word and two words that merely rhyme with ounce; the near-meaning group gathers units of weight and words for a tiny amount.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「十二分之一」一词上的形式，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收重量单位与表示极小量的词。

entries.definition: A unit of length, also descended from Latin uncia, a twelfth part.
entries.definitionCN: 长度单位英寸，同样出自拉丁语 uncia（十二分之一）。

entries.definition: A style of large rounded writing, named from a Latin adjective meaning a twelfth of a foot in height.
entries.definitionCN: 一种大写圆体字，名称出自意为「十二分之一英尺高」的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: To make something known publicly; the ending looks like ounce but the word comes from Latin nuntius, a messenger.
entries.definitionCN: 公开宣告；词尾看似盎司，实际出自拉丁语 nuntius（信使），只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To spring back after hitting a surface; the spelling echoes ounce but the word is probably imitative and unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 碰到表面后弹回；拼写与盎司相近，但一般认为出自模仿声音，来源不同。

entries.definition: A metric unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a kilogram.
entries.definitionCN: 公制重量单位，等于千分之一千克。

entries.definition: A unit of weight made of sixteen ounces, or twelve in the troy system.
entries.definitionCN: 由十六盎司组成的重量单位，金衡制中则为十二盎司。

entries.definition: A very small amount of something that is barely there.
entries.definitionCN: 极少、几乎察觉不到的一点。

entries.definition: An extremely small amount, used especially in negative statements.
entries.definitionCN: 极微小的一点，尤用于否定句。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin fraction, a trade weight and a figure of speech, so its hooks return to cutting, weighing and the smallest measurable share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一个拉丁分数、一个贸易重量和一种说法，记忆钩子都回到切分、称量与最小可称的一份。

normal.en: Uncia meant a twelfth part, so ounce began as a fraction rather than a fixed weight.
normal.cn: uncia 意为十二分之一，所以 ounce 起初是个分数，而不是固定的重量。

normal.en: The same Latin word gave inch, because both were cut from a larger unit by the same habit of dividing into twelve.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词还给出 inch，因为两者都是按十二等分的老习惯从大单位里切出来的。

normal.en: Troy and avoirdupois are two ways of cutting the pound, and ounce simply followed both.
normal.cn: 金衡与常衡是把磅切成两套办法，ounce 两套都跟着用。

normal.en: Kitchen scales read in ounces, which is why the word can mean a very small amount of anything.
normal.cn: 厨房秤以盎司读数，所以这个词可以指任何东西的极小量。

normal.en: An ounce of courage is the unit turned into a moral measure, weighing a quality on the same scale.
normal.cn: an ounce of courage 是把单位变成品性的量尺，用同一杆秤去称一种性情。

abstract.en: A brass scale on a pharmacy counter, one weight on each pan, is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 药铺柜台上一台铜天平、两盘各放一个砝码，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A gold bar on a dealer's tray is the same name made heavier by old custom.
abstract.cn: 经销商托盘上的金条，是同一个名字被旧习惯加重后的样子。

abstract.en: A cook adding a single spoonful to a bowl shows a weight unit shrinking into a pinch.
abstract.cn: 厨师往碗里只加一勺，显示一个重量单位缩成了一撮。

examples.en: The recipe asks for one ounce of butter.
examples.cn: 这份配方要求一盎司黄油。

examples.en: Gold is sold by the troy ounce in most markets.
examples.cn: 多数市场上黄金按金衡盎司出售。

examples.en: He did not show an ounce of regret.
examples.cn: 他没有表现出一丝悔意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盎司」——中文本来就用这两个字音译；称出一小份，正是 ounce。

root: 拉丁语 uncia（十二分之一，也指一种小重量）经古法语 unce 进入英语；同源词还有 inch，因为两者原本都是把一个较大单位切成十二份。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fraction cut from a larger unit; the senses settle that fraction into a trade weight, split it into troy and ordinary measures, then shrink it into a tiny amount and a trace of character.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从较大单位切下的一份；义项先把这个分数落成贸易重量，分成金衡与常衡两种量法，再缩小成极小的数量与一丝品性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small brass scale on a pharmacy counter, a lump of butter on one pan, a tiny weight on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：药铺柜台上的一台小铜天平，一盘放黄油，一盘放小小的砝码。

branches.en: a brass scale on a pharmacy counter
branches.cn: 药铺柜台上的小铜天平

branches.en: a gold bar weighed on a dealer's tray
branches.cn: 经销商托盘上称量的金条

definition_zh: 在外；向外；出去；熄灭；过时；从…出来
definition_en: away from the inside of a place, or moving from within to beyond a boundary; also no longer burning or fashionable; as a preposition, through and away from
core_image: 厨房的灯忽然灭了，一个人摸黑推开门，从屋里走到院子里
scene: 夜里厨房的灯忽然灭了，一个人摸黑推开门，从屋里走到院子里站定。The kitchen light went out while we were still washing the dishes.
sceneCN: 这里 out 是「熄灭」（第 3 个义项：火、灯或电器不再亮、不再工作）；句意为碗还没洗完，厨房的灯就灭了，画面是黑下来的厨房与走向院子的人。

pos.zh: 在外；向外；出去；熄灭；过时
从…出来；离开
过时的；不再流行的

derivatives.zh: 由 out 加比较级词尾 -er 构成，义为「外部的；外面的」
由 out 加 -ing 构成，义为「外出；短途游玩」
由 out 与 set 复合而成，义为「开始；开端」
由 outward 加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向外地」

senses.title: Away from inside a place
senses.definition: not inside a building, room or container, but beyond its boundary
senses.definitionCN: 不在建筑物、房间或容器之内，而处在它的边界之外
senses.example: She is out at the moment, so please call again later.
senses.exampleCN: 她这会儿出去了，请稍后再打。
senses.why: Old English ut simply named the far side of a boundary, so the word's first task is to say that something is not inside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ut 只指边界之外的那一侧，所以这个词最初的任务就是说明某物不在里面；第一义是纯粹的空间否定，没有别的引申。

senses.title: Moving from within to outside
senses.definition: used with verbs of movement to show a passage from inside to beyond
senses.definitionCN: 与表示移动的动词连用，表示从里面穿到外面
senses.example: He walked out without saying a word.
senses.exampleCN: 他一句话没说就走了出去。
senses.why: If the word can name the far side, it can also name the step that reaches it, so verbs of motion take out as a direction.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指界外那一侧，也就能指跨到那一侧的那一步，所以表示移动的动词带上 out 就成了方向；静态位置由此转成动态离开。

senses.title: No longer burning or working
senses.definition: of a fire, lamp or device, no longer burning, shining or running
senses.definitionCN: 指火、灯或电器不再燃烧、不再发亮、不再运转
senses.example: The fire went out before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 火在午夜前就熄了。
senses.why: A flame that is out has left the state of burning, so the word for being beyond a boundary is applied to a condition that has ended.
senses.whyCN: 熄掉的火已经离开了燃烧的状态，于是这个表示「在界外」的词被用到一种已经结束的状态上；熄灭义就是把它从空间之外搬到状态之外。

senses.title: No longer fashionable
senses.definition: of a style or idea, no longer in fashion or no longer accepted
senses.definitionCN: 指样式或观念不再流行，或不再被接受
senses.example: Long skirts are out this season.
senses.exampleCN: 长裙这一季已经过时了。
senses.why: A style that falls outside the set of things people currently accept is literally out of that set, so the spatial word becomes a judgement of taste.
senses.whyCN: 一种样式落在人们当下接受的那一套之外，就字面地「不在这一套里」，于是空间词变成了品味判断；过时义靠的正是「圈外」这个画面。

senses.title: Through and away from
senses.definition: used before a noun, as in out the door or out of the room, to mark the way from inside to outside
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之前，如 out the door 或 out of the room，标出从内到外的路径
senses.example: She ran out the door into the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑出门，冲进了雨里。
senses.why: The preposition keeps the same crossing but puts a noun after it, so out takes an object and names the opening that is passed through.
senses.whyCN: 介词用法保留同一次越界，只在后面接上名词，于是 out 带宾语，指被穿过的那道出口；词性变了，画面没有变。

intro.en: Out is one of the oldest English adverbs, and its history is a single idea, the far side of a boundary, spreading from place to condition and to fashion.
intro.cn: out 是英语最古老的副词之一，它的历史只有一个念头：边界之外的那一侧；这个念头从位置扩展到状态，再扩展到时尚。

items.en: The root usually reconstructed as ud- carried the sense of outward or upward movement, and it is the deepest layer behind the English word.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构为 ud- 的词根带有「向外、向上」的意思，是英语这个词最深的一层。

items.en: The reconstructed ut gave the Germanic languages an adverb for motion away from the inside.
items.cn: 重构形式 ut 为日耳曼诸语提供了一个表示「离开内部」的副词。

items.en: Old English ut was an adverb of place and direction, and it already appeared beside verbs of going and coming.
items.cn: 古英语 ut 是表示位置与方向的副词，已经常与来去的动词连用。

items.en: Middle English out widened from space to conditions, so a fire or a supply could be called out once it had ended.
items.cn: 中古英语把 out 从空间扩展到状态，火或供应一旦终结就可以说成 out。

items.en: Modern English adds the preposition use, the adjective sense of unfashionable, and a large family of compounds from outset to outlook.
items.cn: 现代英语补上介词用法、表示「过时」的形容词义，以及从 outset 到 outlook 的一大族复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the English out and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for the outside position and for leaving.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在英语 out 上的形式，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示外面位置与离开的词。

entries.definition: On or near the outside of something.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物外部或靠近外部的。

entries.definition: A short trip taken for pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 为消遣而进行的短途出游。

entries.definition: To do better than another person.
entries.definitionCN: 做得比另一人更好；胜过。

entries.definition: Concerning, or roughly; the spelling resembles out but the word is built from a different Old English phrase meaning around.

entries.definition: The outer part or surface of something, or beyond the limits of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外部或表面，也指在某个场所的界限之外。

entries.definition: At a distance from a person or place.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某人或某地，处在远处。

entries.definition: In the open air, not inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 在露天，不在建筑物之内。

entries.definition: Towards the outside, or on the outer side.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向外面，或位于外侧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a single boundary picture with many uses, so its hooks return to the far side, the step across it, and the state that lies beyond.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是同一个边界画面的多种用法，记忆钩子都回到界外那一侧、跨过去的那一步，以及落在边界之外的状态。

normal.en: Old English ut marked the far side of a boundary, which is why out answers the plain question where.
normal.cn: 古英语 ut 标出边界的那一侧，所以 out 回答最朴素的「在哪里」。

normal.en: The same word covers the crossing as well as the position, so walk and run take it as a direction.
normal.cn: 同一个词既管位置也管越界，所以 walk 与 run 带上它就成了方向。

normal.en: A fire that has left the state of burning is called out, which shows the word moving from space to condition.
normal.cn: 离开燃烧状态的火被叫作 out，显示这个词从空间挪到了状态。

normal.en: Out of date and out of order share one shape: the thing has fallen outside the set of what still works.
normal.cn: out of date 与 out of order 形状相同：东西落到「还能用」的那一套之外了。

normal.en: Outer, outing and outset all keep the boundary picture, and only the part of speech changes.
normal.cn: outer、outing、outset 都保留着边界画面，变的只是词性。

abstract.en: A door standing open with a lamp still burning inside is the word's plainest picture.
abstract.cn: 一扇门开着、屋里灯还亮着，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A match going dark at the end of a stick is the moment out stops meaning place and starts meaning ended.
abstract.cn: 火柴在棒端熄灭的那一瞬，就是 out 从「位置」转成「结束」的时刻。

abstract.en: A hat left outside a shop window marks a style that has fallen out of favour.
abstract.cn: 一顶被搁在橱窗外的帽子，标记一种已经失宠的样式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬特」——熬到灯都灭了、人还在屋子外面；out 就是在外面，也是熄灭。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the far side of a boundary; the senses move from that position, to the crossing, to a condition that has ended, to a style outside current taste, and to the preposition of passage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是边界之外的那一侧；义项从那个位置，转到跨越动作，转到已经终结的状态，转到落在当下品味之外的样式，再转到表穿越的介词。

definition_zh: 结果；结局；成果；结局指标
definition_en: the result or final situation produced by an event, process, decision, or treatment
core_image: 一条路走到尽头，终点处落下一个清晰的印记
scene: 临床试验结束时，研究团队把两组康复率并排写进同一张表。The main outcome was clear: the treated group recovered twelve points more often than the control group.
sceneCN: 这里 outcome 是“（研究或临床的）结局指标”（第 8 个义项：统计意义上的终点指标）；句意：主要结局指标很清楚：用药组的康复率比对照组高出十二个百分点。图中可辨识物件：病历表、统计柱状图、药瓶、研究记录；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 结果；结局；成果
（研究／医疗）结局指标；终点

derivatives.zh: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的

senses.title: The result of an event or process
senses.definition: the result or final situation that follows from an event or process
senses.definitionCN: 由某个事件或过程产生的最终结果或局面
senses.example: The outcome of the experiment surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 实验的结果让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: The word is a compound of out and come: something comes out of a process and stands at the end of it. The result is pictured as a thing that emerges and becomes visible once the process is finished.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 out 与 come 复合而成：某物从过程里“走出来”，停在过程的末端。结果被想象成一件在过程结束后浮现、变得可见的东西。

senses.title: A consequence of a decision
senses.definition: the effect that a decision or action has, often considered before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 某个决定或行动带来的效果，常在做出决定前就被考虑
senses.example: Before you speak, consider the outcome of your words.
senses.exampleCN: 开口之前，先想想你的话会带来什么后果。
senses.why: The same emergence is now read backwards as consequence: the decision sends something out, and that something returns as the situation you must live in.
senses.whyCN: 同样的“浮现”现在被反向读成后果：决定送出某样东西，而那样东西又作为你必须生活在其中的局面返回。

senses.title: The result of a contest or vote
senses.definition: the final result of an election, trial, game, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 选举、审判、比赛或谈判的最终结果
senses.example: The outcome of the election remained unclear for days.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果数日未明。
senses.why: A contest is a process with a single end point, so outcome fits it naturally. The word does not say who won; it names the shape the whole process leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 竞赛是一个有单一终点的过程，因此 outcome 天然适用。这个词不说明谁赢，只命名整个过程留下的那个形状。

senses.title: A medical or clinical result
senses.definition: the health result of a treatment or illness for a patient or group
senses.definitionCN: 治疗或疾病给患者或群体带来的健康结果
senses.example: Better hygiene led to improved patient outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的卫生条件改善了患者的治疗结果。
senses.why: Medicine turns the everyday word into a measured endpoint: the process is treatment, and what comes out at the end is the patient's condition. The metaphor of emergence becomes a chart.
senses.whyCN: 医学把日常词变成可测量的终点：过程是治疗，末端“走出来”的是患者的状况。浮现的比喻变成了一张图表。

senses.title: The expected or desired result
senses.definition: the result that people hope for or predict, often stated in advance
senses.definitionCN: 人们希望或预测的结果，常被提前说明
senses.example: The negotiators aimed for a fair outcome for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者力求让双方都得到公平的结果。
senses.why: Once the end point is known to be a result, it can be wished for before it exists. The word stops describing what happened and starts naming a target placed at the end of the process.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道末端是一个结果，它就可以在存在之前被期盼。这个词于是不再描述已发生的事，而是命名一个被放在过程末端的目标。

senses.title: A learning outcome in education
senses.definition: a specific skill or understanding that students are expected to gain from a course
senses.definitionCN: 学生预期从课程中获得的具体技能或理解
senses.example: Each lesson lists three learning outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 每节课都列出三项学习成果。
senses.why: Education reverses the direction: instead of asking what came out of teaching, it first declares what should come out. The outcome becomes a designed destination rather than a report.
senses.whyCN: 教育把方向倒过来：不是问教学之后“出来了什么”，而是先声明“应该出来什么”。结果由事后报告变成事先设计的目的地。

senses.title: The result of a legal case
senses.definition: the final decision or settlement of a legal dispute or court case
senses.definitionCN: 法律争议或法庭案件的最终裁决或和解
senses.example: The case outcome depended on one witness.
senses.exampleCN: 案件结果取决于一名证人。
senses.why: A trial is a bounded procedure with an official end, so its result is called an outcome rather than a mere effect. The word suits any process that is formally closed.
senses.whyCN: 审判是一个有官方终点的有限程序，因此它的结果被称为 outcome，而不只是 effect。这个词适用于任何正式结束的过程。

senses.title: A measured endpoint in research
senses.definition: a variable that researchers measure at the end of a study to judge whether an intervention worked
senses.definitionCN: 研究者在研究结束时测量、用来判断干预是否有效的变量
senses.example: Recovery rate was the primary outcome of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 康复率是该试验的主要终点指标。
senses.why: Statistics narrows outcome to one measured thing among many possible results. The end of the process is now a designated variable, chosen before the data are collected so the question cannot be moved afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把 outcome 收窄为众多可能结果中被选定测量的一项。过程的末端现在是一个事先指定的变量，在收集数据前就定好，以免事后移动问题。

intro.en: Outcome is not Latin at all. It is a Scottish English compound of two native words, and its history shows the modern sense is surprisingly late.
intro.cn: outcome 根本不是拉丁词。它是两个英语本族词构成的苏格兰英语复合词，其历史显示现代义出现得相当晚。

items.en: c. 1200, out-coming was used for 'an emergence, act or fact of coming out'. Old English had utancumen 'stranger, foreigner', literally 'one who came from outside'.
items.cn: 约 1200 年，out-coming 表示“出现、出来的行为或事实”。古英语有 utancumen“陌生人、外来者”，字面是“从外面来的人”。

items.en: The noun outcome is recorded in 1788, originally Scottish, meaning 'that which results from something'. It comes from the verbal phrase out + come.
items.cn: 名词 outcome 记录于 1788 年，最初见于苏格兰，义为“由某事物产生的结果”。它来自动词短语 out + come。

items.en: Popularized in English by Thomas Carlyle around the 1830s, according to standard references.
items.cn: 据通行资料，托马斯·卡莱尔在 1830 年代前后使这个词在英语中流行开来。

items.en: The word stays a transparent compound: out (forth, into view) + come (arrive). Its force is that the result is something that came out and can now be seen.
items.cn: 这个词始终是透明的复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（到达）。它的力量在于：结果是“走出来”、现在能被看见的东西。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine, education, and statistics turned outcome into a countable endpoint: patient outcome, learning outcome, primary outcome.
items.cn: 20 世纪的医学、教育与统计学把 outcome 变成可计数的终点：patient outcome、learning outcome、primary outcome。

note.en: The first group separates other out- compounds; the second ranks the main synonyms by where they place the result.
note.cn: 第一组把其他 out- 复合词分开；第二组按“结果被放在哪里”来区分主要近义词。

entries.definition: the amount produced by a machine, worker, or system. It is what is put out, not the situation that results.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、工人或系统的产出量。它是“被放出来的量”，不是最终形成的局面。

entries.definition: the sudden start of disease, war, or violence. It names a breaking out, not a result.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病、战争或暴力的突然爆发。它指“破壳而出”，不是结果。

entries.definition: a view or forecast. It is what you look out at, or forward to, not what came out.
entries.definitionCN: 景色；前景展望。它是你向外看、向前看的东西，不是出来的结果。

entries.definition: what happens because of something else. It is the broadest term and can name anything from a sum to a consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 因另一事物而发生的事。它是最宽泛的词，可以指从计算结果到后果的任何东西。

entries.definition: a result that follows logically or causally, often with a sense of importance or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 按逻辑或因果随之而来的结果，常含重要性或责任意味。

entries.definition: the change produced by a cause. It stresses the change itself rather than the final situation.
entries.definitionCN: 原因造成的变化。它强调变化本身，而不是最终局面。

entries.definition: the final or eventual result of a series of events. It is informal and stresses the end of a long story.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列事件最终的结局。它较口语化，强调一个长故事的最后收束。

normalIntro.en: Five spelling hooks, then three abstract pictures of a process arriving at its end.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个拼写钩子，再用三个“过程抵达终点”的抽象画面。

normal.en: out + come: what comes out at the end.
normal.cn: out + come：最后“走出来”的那个东西。

normal.en: outcome ends in -come just as become: something becomes visible at the end.
normal.cn: outcome 和 become 一样以 -come 结尾：某物在最后变得可见。

normal.en: An election outcome is the scoreboard after the last vote is counted.
normal.cn: 选举的 outcome 就是最后一张票计完后那块记分牌。

normal.en: Learning outcomes are written before the course, like a destination on a ticket.
normal.cn: learning outcomes 写在课程之前，像车票上的目的地。

normal.en: Primary outcome is the one number a trial promises to report.
normal.cn: primary outcome 是一项试验承诺要报告的那个数字。

abstract.en: An outcome is the shape a process leaves behind after it stops moving.
abstract.cn: 结果是过程停止运动后留下的那个形状。

abstract.en: You can design an outcome without being able to control it: the end is a target, not a guarantee.
abstract.cn: 你可以设计一个结果，却无法控制它：终点是目标，不是保证。

abstract.en: Every decision sends something out into the world, and that something comes back as the room you live in.
abstract.cn: 每个决定都往世界里送出某样东西，而那样东西会作为你居住的房间返回。

examples.en: No one could predict the outcome of the talks.
examples.cn: 没有人能预测会谈的结果。

examples.en: The study measured three outcomes: pain, mobility, and sleep quality.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了三个结局指标：疼痛、活动能力与睡眠质量。

examples.en: A good process does not always produce a good outcome.
examples.cn: 好的过程并不总能产生好的结果。

dict_mnemonic.note: 记成“从过程里走出来（out）并到达（come）的东西”。
dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ come（来）→ 出来的结果 → 结果、结局

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（来）；1788 年见于苏格兰英语，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from any result, to consequences and contest results, then to measured endpoints in medicine, education, law, and statistics.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从任何“结果”出发，走到后果与比赛结果，再到医学、教育、法律与统计中可测量的终点。

core.en: A path reaching its end, where a mark is left behind
core.cn: 一条路走到尽头，在那里留下一个印记

branches.en: General result: what an event or process finally produced.
branches.cn: 一般结果：一个事件或过程最终产生的东西。

branches.en: Formal endings: the result of a contest, or of a legal case.
branches.cn: 正式终点：比赛的结果，或案件的结果。

branches.en: Measured endings: a patient's health result, or a study's primary endpoint.
branches.cn: 可测量的终点：患者的健康结果，或研究的主要终点。

branches.en: Ends declared in advance: a hoped-for result, or a learning outcome.
branches.cn: 事先声明的终点：期望的结果，或学习成果。

branches.en: Consequence: the word looks back at what a decision cost.
branches.cn: 后果：这个词回看一个决定付出了什么代价。

intro.en: Outcome belongs to the huge out- family and the even larger come family. Both halves are native English, so there is no Latin root here.
intro.cn: outcome 属于庞大的 out- 词族，也属于更大的 come 词族。两半都是英语本族词，因此这里没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: out is Old English ut, from Proto-Germanic *ut-, and come is Old English cuman, from Proto-Germanic *kwem-.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：out 是古英语 ut，来自原始日耳曼语 *ut-；come 是古英语 cuman，来自原始日耳曼语 *kwem-。

items.meaning: that which comes out of a process
items.example: The outcome was better than expected.
The outcoming of the vote was delayed.
items.exampleCN: 投票结果的公布被推迟了。

items.meaning: to move toward and arrive at a point

items.example: Her income doubled after the promotion.
items.exampleCN: 升职后她的收入翻了一倍。

items.meaning: to get over an obstacle and win through
items.example: They overcame the shortage of funds.

items.meaning: about to come; willing to give information
items.meaningCN: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的
items.example: The forthcoming report will cover the trial.
items.exampleCN: 即将发布的报告将涵盖这项试验。

items.meaning: an arrival; the approach of something
items.example: The coming of winter changed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 冬天的到来改变了计划。

items.meaning: to come to be; to grow into
a variable used to judge a result in research
items.example: Pain score was the main outcome measure.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛评分是主要的结局测量指标。
